page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 1 physical core with 2 threads. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local NVMe SSD storage and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% due to the limited dual-vCPU configuration. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth in the bottom 10% and large block read/write bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, deliver average performance.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. However, it exhibits poor performance in database operations, software compilation, and ray tracing. The instance is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, single-threaded text processing, and small-scale web serving where a dedicated AMD EPYC core is beneficial but multi-core throughput is not critical.
